chapter: After the Paradise: club dates and Virginia
title: His singing: scat, ballads and show songs
summary: He had to sing on club dates, started scat singing at the Paradise, then tried Embraceable You and Timmy Rogers's songs, with blues coming later.

story.theme_name: Singers and the musicians who accompanied them

blocks.x: Before they go too far down here, let's...what had become some of the standard numbers that you would do in a...if it was up to you to call the shots...both in terms of your horn and...did you, in fact, still continue singing?
Oh yeah, I had to do that

with them club dates. Oh yeah. That was one of the main reasons they hired me. To entertain, you see. Then I began to learn more songs. But I picked songs that I could sing because, you know, I'm not a singer and the people liked it. You know, standard songs like "Birth of the Blues" and of course when "Hello Dolly" and them things came out, you know, you do them things 'cause the public liked those things.
Yeah. I'm thinking of some of the...I guess what I wanted to do is trace, for a minute, your history of doing vocals.

Yeah, well I started scatting in the Paradise because the people liked it, they thought it was funny. Then I ventured out and I started singin' "Embraceable You". I think that was my first ballad. (laughter) And then I did "You're a Weaver of Dreams". This all comes back to me now. And then I did one of Timmy Rodgers' songs, "Ohh, Whatcha Doin' to Me" and that was it for a little while. (laughter) But they liked it.

I wasn't into the blues then. You know, I was just scat singing. I played it a little, but I wasn't into it, you know. That came later, you know. You get a little older, you know. You know, because you be into jazz, purely jazz, you like blues singers, but your mind is on your horn. You see what I mean. So I was aware of vocalists, you know, but I was involved in my horn, you see. But as I said before, to hold a job and to make a livin' you learn that you have to do a lot of things, you know, so that's how I started singin', yeah. Then I used to do, 'That Old Black Magic,' yeah. I'm thinkin' now, (laughter) you know it was things like that.
